newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australia, Thailand seek to double trade.
newsitem.headline: Australia, Thailand seek to double trade.

text.p: Australia and Thailand on Thursday agreed to attack trade obstacles between the two countries in a bid to double trade by the turn of the century.

Foreign and trade ministers meeting in Canberra agreed to move on obstacles such as quarantine regulations and said they would set up industry groups to foster trade and investment to double trade from the A$2.8 billion (US$2.2 billion) in the year to June 30, 1996.
"I am confident we will be able to meet this target," Australian Foreign Minister Alexander Downer told reporters.

Downer and Trade Minister Tim Fischer, who is also deputy prime minister, met Thai Foreign Minister Prachaub Chaiyasarn and Commerce Minister Narongchai Akrasanee for two days of talks, the latest in a series of bilateral forums Australia has established with the booming economies of neighbouring Asia.
"The (meeting)...produced concrete results with practical benefits for exporters, consumers and others in both countries," Bangkok and Canberra said in a joint statement.
"These include breakthroughs in intellectual property, business co-operation, people-to-people links and political support and significantly better understanding of quarantine approval processes."
The two countries signed a memorandum of understanding to boost co-operation on intellectual property right issues, including information exchange and monitoring.
Downer also announced a A$500,000 programme to allow young Australian graduates to live and work in Thailand.
